title: Set useful limits
summary: A constraint is a rule the output should follow. Choose limits that serve the reader, such as a short length or a required explanation.
introduction: A constraint is a rule the output should follow. Choose limits that serve the reader, such as a short length or a required explanation. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A constraint is a rule the output should follow. Choose limits that serve the reader, such as a short length or a required explanation.

blocks.code:
Task: explain evaporation.
Limits: at most four sentences; explain the word vapour; include one example with a wet cloth.
blocks.title: Set useful limits

blocks.text: These limits make the explanation easier to review. If four sentences are too few for a clear accurate answer, revise the limits thoughtfully.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Write two checks that a reviewer can apply to the reply.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Avoid conflicting instructions, such as exactly one word and a detailed paragraph.
For more detail later, use this [Prompt Engineering further reading](https://www.promptingguide.ai/introduction).
